title: Incremental Improvement (Kaizen)
hook: Overhauling everything every quarter is exhausting. Tiny weekly tweaks are what actually stick.
statement: Small, frequent improvements compound into big results over time.
explainer: A 1% gain feels like nothing this week. Stack it every week and by year end you're in a different league, without the burnout of a huge overhaul.
sop: Pick one piece of a recurring process, not the whole thing.
Make one small change you can test.
Measure before and after with the same metric.
Work out the percent change. Keep it if positive, drop it if not.
Repeat weekly on a different piece.
equation_example: Current is 100, improvement is 1%. 100 × (1 + 0.01) = 101. Do that every week and it adds up fast. Higher means the tweak is working. Zero or negative means undo it, no guilt.
question: Write down one 1% improvement you can make this week to something you do every week.
closing_statement: Small and frequent beats big and rare.
